narrative.overview: The illustrations are the light source of the whole game; interface surfaces recede into warm umber and wine shadows, framed by hairline gold. It should feel warm, comforting, mysterious and magical, never overwhelming. Outside the story the game is the illuminated grimoire: an open book on a dark, candlelit desk, with silk ribbons for navigation and every section a two-page parchment spread.

rules.name: Light has a source
rules.body: Glow and warm bloom only on light sources (lantern, candles, sunset, spells, title) and special moments. Everything else uses neutral shadow.

rules.name: Gold is jewellery
rules.body: Thin lines, small caps labels, vines, the diamond. Never fills, never paragraphs.

rules.name: No gradient text, ever
rules.body: Solid cream or ink; warmth comes from light behind, not colour inside letters.

rules.name: The Red Ink Rule
rules.body: Rubric marks what is dated, current or chosen: a day, a label, the place you stand. It never fills a box.

rules.name: No eyebrows
rules.body: A heading stands alone; a page label never sits above a title as a kicker.

rules.name: One page, one h1
rules.body: Page titles are h1, card and person titles h2; headings never skip a level.

dos: Let illustrations carry colour; keep chrome quiet.
Use the vine flourish for primary and focused actions only.
Keep story text on solid backing with AA contrast in every mode.
On the grimoire, write numbers the way a book would ("Chapter one of eight"; friendship as "Friendship 40 of 100" in a tooltip, not "40/100").
Keep the day's closing actions in the page foot.
donts: Glow on everything, gradient text, purple/blue neon, glass cards everywhere, icon-card grids.
Animate trees, mountains, rocks, the castle or the lantern in the opening, or anything by displacing detailed pixels.
Use gold for paragraphs or wide tracking on body text.
Put kickers above headings, solid colour fills on calendar days, or chromatic shadows on the page (glow belongs to the desk's light sources).
Repeat the same person or card twice on one spread.
